deepdive.sec: IT Services — Enterprise AI, Decision Intelligence & Platform-led Modernization

bull_bear.body: Investment is being deliberately front-run: "We will continue to invest in platform capacity ahead of demand with full visibility into the return. The deal ramp costs are the predictable leading indicator of the revenue growth that follows." Inorganic activity is a steady drumbeat of small customer-contract acquisitions at 1x–1.2x revenue rather than large M&A — Aravind Viswanathan noted pointedly, "this is not a $1 billion acquisition." No dividend or buyback discussion on this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Macro is explicitly acknowledged: "There is always a chance that macro will get really harsh, much harsher. And if we get an interest rate shock on top of the oil shock, then that will create disruption in the economy."
- Margin is near the bottom of the guided band after absorbing acquisition costs — the band holds only if utilisation reverses as promised.
- OCF conversion at 80% of net income is roughly half the industry norm on an OCF/EBITDA basis; the fix is deferred to FY28.
- Red Oak has not consummated; the timing slipped into end-August/early-September and it will not contribute a full quarter in Q2.
- Insurance and Logistics both declined sequentially. Insurance is explained by milestone completion; Logistics is a genuine macro problem in a shrinking unit.
- Hedge losses persist and will take a couple of quarters to reflect in operating margin.
- Structural view worth flagging: management believes traditional discretionary spend will not return to prior form — "I don't think we will see discretionary spend come back in a way that it used to be 3/4/5 years ago", and that "long-term annuity run deals… are highly susceptible to disruption."
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Nitin Rakesh is the most conceptually assertive voice on this batch of calls — he coined and defended a category ("the Agency Gap", "Enterprise Agency") and drew a sharp line against agentic AI as sold by platform vendors: "Agentic AI, as shipped by every major platform vendor, is not the answer… agentic AI is a capability. Enterprise Agency is an outcome." He was also willing to be concrete about what he *doesn't* know — declining to quantify full-year contribution from contract acquisitions because "we don't have visibility to do all the deals that might come up." Aravind Viswanathan gave a clean, specific margin walk and did not dodge the OCF criticism, conceding "you are right" before explaining. One notable barb at peers: some companies "are forward-forecasting 60%, 70% productivity in outer years because they think that AI will enable that. They just haven't figured out how to."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The falling TCV-to-revenue correlation (0.9 → 0.74) is being reported as a positive, and the logic holds: shorter-burst, deployment-ready deals convert faster, which decouples the ratio. Worth tracking whether revenue actually follows.
- The TAP deal structure — two-thirds of consideration as earn-out running through the P&L — means the margin drag is a multi-year, mechanical item, not a one-off transaction cost. Aravind explicitly said there was no meaningful transaction cost.
- OKIN outgrew its own LOI ($4 mn revenue in one quarter vs $5.5 mn total contract value including contingent consideration) — evidence that these "land and expand" contract acquisitions are not static books.
- Management's view on model commoditisation is directionally important for the whole sector: "the real revolution is not going to be in what model you're using. It's going to get commoditized fairly quickly" — the money is in the stack that lets an enterprise ingest whatever comes next.
- Budget is moving outside the CIO: "there are additional pockets of spend that sit outside of tech because if you show them a business case that we can expand revenue conversion by 1%… that business case gets funded, whether there is tech budget or no."
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Commits to a stated operating-margin band of 14.75%-15.75% as the framing constraint on growth investment and acquisition absorption, rather than chasing volume at any margin.
- Targets 80% conversion of net income into operating cash flow as an explicit, repeatable cash-discipline benchmark.
- Working capital is a watch item: DSO on the combined debtors plus contract-assets basis has risen to about 95 days, with contract assets up roughly 17 days YoY as platform/outcome-linked contracts grow.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **BFS:** stable, eight quarters of structural growth, compound quarterly growth over 3.5% — described as the strongest among peers.
- **Insurance:** grew ~35% in FY26; the sequential dip reflects project milestone completions, not client loss — "We have no client impact to call out as we stand." Expected to be a key FY27 growth driver.
- **Logistics & Transportation:** genuinely headwinded by macro and geopolitics; now a small unit where "small number changes drive high percentage variations." More work to be done here and in Airlines and Railroads.
- **TMT:** returned to strong growth as recent deal wins ramped.
- **Customer-contract acquisitions (OKIN, Red Oak):** these are vendor-consolidation deals, not M&A — no entity is taken over, but the accounting follows acquisition accounting with the consideration almost entirely customer relationships and intangibles. Typical consideration is 1x–1.2x revenue. OKIN delivered close to $4 mn of revenue in Q1 against a total contract value including contingent consideration of $5.5 mn — i.e. it already outgrew the original LOI assumption.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **A defined "right to win" at a specific intersection:** "this problem sits at the intersection of brownfield enterprise complexity, integration depth, domain-specific decision intelligence, and governance — precisely the territory we have built over thirty years. Not many AI-native startups can replicate that context. Not many hyperscalers want to own that accountability."
- **Refusal to compete on price:** "we are not competing on price because that's a game that we really don't want to play… that price discounting game only works when you're doing effort-based pricing. But when you change the equation and do outcome-based pricing, it really doesn't make any sense for clients to look at it that way."
- **Demand compression as evidence:** "within seven weeks of platform launch, multiple opportunities moved from conversation to closure and are now moving to execution. That is not a normal sales cycle."
- **BFS depth:** eight consecutive quarters of >3.5% compound quarterly growth, and 100% YoY BFS pipeline growth, in a period when peers report BFS caution.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Frames a 'validated market gap': enterprises own data and AI pilots but have no governed way to turn them into accountable decisions, and Mphasis TRIA is pitched as the bridge from AI investment to measurable economic outcomes.
- Claims a defensible right to win on four fronts - brownfield (legacy) complexity, decision intelligence, execution capability and governance - arguing 'Enterprise Agency has to be built and cannot be bought', which favours integrators over pure product vendors.
- Describes compounding platform economics: land in one decision loop, prove measurable gain, then expand as platform reuse compounds with each deployment, creating new addressable penetration inside existing clients.
- Self-describes as a Hi-Tech, Hi-Touch, Hi-Trust, engineering-DNA company with human-in-the-loop intelligence and a customer-centric Front2Back transformation framework serving marquee global enterprises.
- Reads client demand as shifting from AI experimentation to accountable enterprise outcomes, where value must be durable and measurable and integration/execution capability is the differentiator.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The deck notes margins were delivered within the stated band 'after absorbing the acquisition costs', confirming an inorganic addition in the period, but names no target, price or rationale.
- [Demand mix] Growth leadership is rotating - TMT and Retail led, GCC (global capability centre) mandates drove ROW, while Logistics & Transportation contracted sharply, indicating deliberate diversification away from a BFS-only story even as BFS Direct compounds at 3.5%+ CQGR over eight quarters.
- [Delivery mix] Legacy ITO is shrinking while APPS and BPO grow, showing a structural shift of revenue mix toward AI-led modernization and platform-linked operations.
- [Risk disclosure] Safe-harbour language flags heavy dependence on US clients, industry-segment concentration, Indian wage inflation, immigration restrictions, fixed-price contract overruns and acquisition-integration risk as the standing structural risks.
- [Guidance] FY27 outlook of high single-digit to low double-digit growth with Q2 expected to be the best sequential constant-currency growth in three years.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Two identifiable drags this quarter, one recurring and one reversing. The TAP earn-out (~0.35%) flows through the P&L rather than purchase accounting and persists over the next couple of years. The utilisation drop was a conscious pre-build for Q2 growth and reverses. Management expects gross-margin expansion opportunity as platform adoption and attach rate show up "over the next 2 to 3 quarters", with the reinvest-versus-retain split an open decision. On the contract-acquisition deals, the upfront is almost entirely expensed and the deal is underwritten to be profitable in line with company average *after* that expensing — "We are not trying to buy low-margin businesses that we need to transform."
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue $471 mn (+2.1% QoQ, +8.3% YoY cc); Direct $465 mn (+9.9% YoY cc). Net new TCV $461 mn — fifth straight quarter above $400 mn; TTM TCV >$1.8 bn; three large deals, one >$100 mn; 63% of TCV AI-led. EBIT margin −60 bps (TAP earn-out ~0.35% + deliberate utilisation drop). EPS INR 25.6 (−4% QoQ). OCF $39 mn; DSO 95 days. Pipeline at all-time high, 2.8x since Mphasis.ai, +8% QoQ / +28% YoY; AI-led deals 70% of pipeline; BFS pipeline +100% YoY. Tria launched and closing inside seven weeks. FY27 guidance and 14.75–15.75% margin band both maintained; Q2 guided to best sequential cc growth in three years.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did Q2 actually deliver the best sequential cc growth in three years (the single most falsifiable claim on this call); did the utilisation drag reverse and margin move off the band's lower half; Red Oak consummation by end-Aug/early-Sep; Insurance sequential recovery and margin normalisation; DSO trending down from 95 days; OCF conversion tracking to 80% of net income._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** FY27 **maintained** at high single-digit to low double-digit growth in constant currency, "despite the uncertain macro environment." Red Oak is already baked into this range.
- **Q2 specifically:** "Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years."
- **Margin:** FY27 EBIT within the band of **14.75% to 15.75%** — "not because we are defending a floor, but because we are making deliberate platform investments while holding financial discipline."
- **Cash conversion:** operating cash flow conversion expected to remain at **80% of net income through FY27**, with normalisation of the OCF/EBITDA ratio from **FY28** as upfront investments in large deals begin to be recovered.
- **DSO:** to improve progressively through the remainder of the year.
- **Red Oak:** consummation expected end of August / early September 2026 — contract assignment and employee takeover in progress; will not carry a full-quarter impact in Q2.
- **Insurance margin:** transformation-programme ramp costs to normalise over the next two quarters.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Total pipeline grew 8% sequentially and 28% YoY to an all-time high, and is 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch. Composition: non-BFS pipeline +18% QoQ; large deals (>$20 mn) pipeline +10% QoQ; BFS pipeline +100% YoY. AI-led deals have gone from 12% to 70% of pipeline and are "now stabilizing" — management's read is that AI is no longer a deal type but the way the company competes across all verticals and sizes. Modernization and Everything-as-a-Platform are the fastest-growing solution archetypes, mapping directly to the newly launched product lines. The TTM TCV-to-revenue correlation fell from >0.9 to ~0.74, which management explained as a *feature*: short-burst, deployment-led deals consume within one or two quarters, and foundation-building work completes in 12–16 weeks before scale deployment waves follow.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: The platform thesis rests on Tria: Modernize builds "enterprise memory" by extracting structured context from systems, rules, workflows and process history; Optimize then uses that memory to improve decision loops across revenue, pricing, demand, supply chain and risk. The commercial consequence management is pointing at is revenue quality — ARR and managed services now being bundled together in Tria deals, Tria influencing large deals at the *evaluation* stage as a proof point, and new addressable penetration at existing clients opening budget pools that were inaccessible under the service-led model. The FDE (forward deployed engineer) motion is small pods of 3–5 elite engineers at high billing rates whose job is to deliver proof of value and hand over to scale delivery — management was explicit that the value is the platform deployment and subsequent managed-services stickiness, not the FDE margin itself.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Q1 is a foundation quarter — revenue $471 mn, +2.1% QoQ and +8.3% YoY in constant currency, with margin down 60 bps on deal-ramp costs and the TAP acquisition earn-out. The signal is the pipeline: 2.8x since the Mphasis.ai launch and at an all-time high, with AI-led deals now 70% of it, and the newly launched Tria platform closing multiple opportunities within seven weeks. Management guided Q2 to "the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years" while holding the FY27 range and margin band unchanged.

risks.note: Management states 'Americas is our prime market, and this geography contributed 83.5% of our revenues in FY26', and the BRSR discloses that 'Mphasis Limited's export sales percentage is 90% for FY26'. A demand, policy or tariff shock in the United States therefore transmits almost directly to the top line; the Board's Report flags that trade tariffs and macroeconomic uncertainty are already prompting enterprises to scrutinise technology spending more carefully.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in the Americas / export dependence

risks.note: The MD&A states 'Banking and Financial Services and Insurance segments comprise 67.0% of our overall revenue', with BFS the declared focus vertical. Two-thirds of revenue is exposed to a single macro-sensitive client industry whose technology budgets tighten with credit conditions — which the MD&A notes are among the channels through which the Middle East conflict is introducing uncertainty.
risks.risk: Vertical concentration in Banking, Financial Services and Insurance

risks.note: The BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — computer programming activities (IT consultancy, information and communication services). There is no diversifying business line to offset a downturn in enterprise IT services demand.

The MD&A states the global economy is 'entering a period of elevated and broadening risks', with OECD projecting global GDP growth slowing from 3.2% in 2025 to 2.9% in 2026 and the escalation of the Middle East conflict entirely negating earlier upward revisions, creating uncertainty across supply chains, commodity prices and credit conditions. It cites McKinsey's March 2026 outlook noting geopolitical instability 'is now the most-cited threat to enterprise growth'.

Reported growth is materially inflated by currency: 'During the year Indian Rupee depreciated 5.3% against USD. Adjusting for the Rupee depreciation, overall gross revenue grew 6.7% in FY26' versus 12.6% reported. The Results of Operations table also carries a 'Profit / (loss) on cash flow hedges reclassified to revenue' line, indicating hedging exposure between gross and net revenue.

The Board's Report concedes that 'the path from potential to value is harder than it looks' — most enterprise AI investment is stalled at the information-processing layer, enterprises struggle to organise information for AI, and 'most such programmes stall or fail before they deliver value'. Mphasis' AI-led pipeline and platform investments (Tria, NeoIP, Ontosphere) are underwritten by clients successfully crossing that gap; management also frames a competitive fault line between 'companies that service AI' and 'companies that deploy it'.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the AI-led transformation thesis

risks.note: The company is deliberately shrinking its DXC channel ('We continue to de-risk DXC business, the revenues from which declined 14.8%'), while Infrastructure Services revenue declined and Logistics & Transportation fell sharply as a share of the business. Growth therefore depends entirely on new-customer ramp-ups and wallet-share gains in the Direct business offsetting these run-offs.
risks.risk: Structurally declining legacy revenue pools and channel de-risking

risks.note: The MD&A notes industry-wide changes in labour composition and reliance on 'large-scale upskilling of the workforce in AI', while the FY26 P&L carried an exceptional item described as 'towards impact of change in labour laws' — evidencing that statutory employment-cost changes flow directly to the company. Cost of revenues is dominated by direct people costs, so wage and utilisation dynamics drive margin.
